name: Household Ledger - Recommendation Agent (SCAFFOLD, not deployed)

parameters.content:
## SCAFFOLD — NOT DEPLOYED
Implements household-ledger-architecture.md §7 (bulk-trip economics) — the 4th of the 5 planned agents. Unlike the other three scaffolds, no schema extension is needed: `Stores` and `Inventory.cycle_count` are already in household-ledger-sheets-schema.md.

WHY THIS CAN'T PRODUCE REAL OUTPUT YET, EVEN ONCE DEPLOYED: it needs real `Stores.distance_from_home_mi`/`est_trip_cost` data (Open Decision #5 — manual entry to start, per the doc's own recommendation) and real `Inventory.avg_days_to_finish`/`cycle_count` history, which only accumulates once the Check-In Agent has actually been running for multiple purchase cycles. That's expected — this is the same 'drafted before its dependencies exist' situation as the other three scaffolds.

V1 SIMPLIFICATION, FLAGGED HONESTLY: architecture.md says trip cost should be 'amortized if the bulk buy covers several months of supply' — true multi-item trip-bundling (combining several items' savings to justify one trip) is a harder optimization problem than this scaffold solves. V1 rule: recommend only if a SINGLE item's own annual savings already exceeds one round trip's cost on its own — conservative (will under-recommend relative to true trip-bundling economics), but won't give a false-positive recommendation.

SETUP TODOs: replace `documentId`/credential placeholders; connect Telegram (Open Decision #3, same question as the other Telegram-using scaffolds). The 'show as a badge in the app next to that item' idea in architecture.md §7 step 4 is a src/App.jsx frontend change — not touched here, flagged as a separate follow-on task.
